components.statement: The polyfill package is MIT "except ES6 ports of browserify modules which are whatever the original library was"; its events.js is a port of Node.js's lib/events.js, so Node.js's licence is given too.
components.evidence: NOT prebuilt by the plan's marker rule (no __webpack_require__, define.amd or wasmBinary): a rollup build that inlines another package with no runtime left. Found through its sibling source map. Map source ../../../../node_modules/rollup-plugin-node-polyfills/polyfills/events.js, byte-identical to that file in the 0.2.1 tarball. Ketcher lockfile: node_modules/rollup-plugin-node-polyfills 0.2.1. The file is byte-identical to src/es6/events.js in rollup-plugin-node-builtins 2.1.2 (Calvin Metcalf; package.json says ISC; no licence file), which the polyfill package forked. It has no header; its code is Node.js's lib/events.js of the v6/v7 era turned into an ES module (45 differing lines against v7.0.0, 65 against v6.0.0). Node.js v7.0.0's lib/events.js has no per-file header, so the Node text is lines 1-50 of Node.js's LICENSE at tag v7.0.0 (the Node.js and Joyent MIT grants, up to the list of Node's own bundled libraries, which do not apply), copied byte for byte.
